label: Population, 2021 Census
description: Total population counted in the 2021 Census for the place's census metropolitan area / agglomeration (or provincial part of Ottawa–Gatineau; Iqaluit is the city itself).
basis: 100% data; total population, 2021 boundaries; counts are randomly rounded to a multiple of 5 only for small areas
comparabilityNote: Compares CMA/CA populations (not city-proper populations). Ottawa and Gatineau are the Ontario and Quebec parts of one CMA. Iqaluit is a single municipality, not a CA.

label: Population change, 2016 to 2021
description: Percentage change in census population between the 2016 and 2021 censuses, on 2021 geographic boundaries.
basis: 100% data; (2021 count − 2016 count on 2021 boundaries) ÷ 2016 count; computed from published counts
comparabilityNote: Census counts, not July estimates; undercoverage differs by census year.

label: Immigrants, share of population
description: Share of the population in private households who are or have ever been landed immigrants or permanent residents (immigrant status).
basis: 25% sample data (long-form census), so values carry sampling variability and random rounding; universe: population in private households; non-permanent residents are in the denominator and not counted as immigrants; computed from counts
comparabilityNote: Share of the CMA/CA population, not of the city proper.

label: Recent immigrants (2016 to 2021), share of population
description: Share of the population in private households who immigrated between 2016 and 2021 (admitted up to 11 May 2021).
basis: 25% sample data (long-form census), so values carry sampling variability and random rounding; universe: population in private households; computed from counts
comparabilityNote: Immigrants who arrived in 2016–2021 and were still living there in May 2021; not admissions or intended destinations.

label: Knows French (French only or English and French)
description: Share of the population who can conduct a conversation in French (French only, or English and French), among all ages.
basis: 25% sample data (long-form census), so values carry sampling variability and random rounding; universe: population in private households, all ages; knowledge of official languages; computed from counts
comparabilityNote: Self-reported conversational ability; includes children. Ottawa and Gatineau use provincial-part values.

label: Knows both English and French
description: Share of the population who can conduct a conversation in both official languages (English-French bilingualism), among all ages.
basis: 25% sample data (long-form census), so values carry sampling variability and random rounding; universe: population in private households, all ages; computed from counts
comparabilityNote: Self-reported; includes children. Ottawa and Gatineau use provincial-part values.

label: Non-official language spoken most often at home
description: Share of the population whose language spoken most often at home is a single non-official language (excludes multiple-language answers such as English and a non-official language).
basis: 25% sample data (long-form census), so values carry sampling variability and random rounding; universe: population in private households, all ages; single-response 'Non-official language'; computed from counts
comparabilityNote: Understates use of other languages at home because multiple-language households are counted separately.

label: Commute mainly by public transit
description: Share of workers whose main mode of commuting is public transit (bus, subway, light rail, commuter train or ferry).
basis: 25% sample data (long-form census), so values carry sampling variability and random rounding; universe: employed labour force aged 15+ with a usual place of work (excludes those working at home and with no fixed workplace); computed from counts
comparabilityNote: Census was taken in May 2021 during COVID-19 restrictions, which lowered transit use and raised work from home; compare with caution to earlier censuses.

label: Commute mainly by car, truck or van
description: Share of workers whose main mode of commuting is car, truck or van (as driver or passenger).
basis: 25% sample data (long-form census), so values carry sampling variability and random rounding; universe: employed labour force aged 15+ with a usual place of work; computed from counts
comparabilityNote: May 2021 (pandemic) conditions; excludes people working at home.

label: Commute mainly walking or cycling
description: Share of workers whose main mode of commuting is active transportation (walked or bicycle).
basis: 25% sample data (long-form census), so values carry sampling variability and random rounding; universe: employed labour force aged 15+ with a usual place of work; walked + bicycle; computed from counts
comparabilityNote: May 2021 (pandemic) conditions; excludes people working at home.

label: Commute of 45 minutes or more
description: Share of workers whose usual one-way commuting duration is 45 minutes or more.
basis: 25% sample data (long-form census), so values carry sampling variability and random rounding; universe: employed labour force aged 15+ with a usual place of work; (45–59 + 60+ minutes) ÷ total; computed from counts
comparabilityNote: Self-reported usual one-way duration, May 2021.

label: Average household size
description: Average number of persons per private household (population in private dwellings ÷ private dwellings occupied by usual residents), persons per household.
basis: 100% data; computed from published counts of population in private dwellings and occupied private dwellings
comparabilityNote: Computed average (published counts); may differ in the last decimal from StatCan's own rounded average.

Values are for the climate station chosen to represent the place (flag station_proxy), not for the whole city. Stations differ in elevation, distance to water and urban setting. All use the 1991-2020 normals period.
label: January mean daily temperature (1991–2020 normal)
description: Average of daily mean temperatures in January, 1991–2020 climate normal at the representative station.
basis: ECCC climate normal; monthly mean of daily mean temperature

comparabilityNote: Values are for the climate station chosen to represent the place (flag station_proxy), not for the whole city. Stations differ in elevation, distance to water and urban setting. All use the 1991-2020 normals period.
label: July mean daily temperature (1991–2020 normal)

basis: ECCC climate normal; monthly mean of daily mean temperature

comparabilityNote: Values are for the climate station chosen to represent the place (flag station_proxy), not for the whole city. Stations differ in elevation, distance to water and urban setting. All use the 1991-2020 normals period.
label: January mean daily minimum temperature (1991–2020 normal)
description: Average of daily minimum temperatures in January (typical overnight low), 1991–2020 normal.
basis: ECCC climate normal; monthly mean of daily minimum temperature

comparabilityNote: Values are for the climate station chosen to represent the place (flag station_proxy), not for the whole city. Stations differ in elevation, distance to water and urban setting. All use the 1991-2020 normals period.
label: July mean daily maximum temperature (1991–2020 normal)
description: Average of daily maximum temperatures in July (typical afternoon high), 1991–2020 normal.
basis: ECCC climate normal; monthly mean of daily maximum temperature

comparabilityNote: Values are for the climate station chosen to represent the place (flag station_proxy), not for the whole city. Stations differ in elevation, distance to water and urban setting. All use the 1991-2020 normals period.
label: Annual precipitation (1991–2020 normal)
description: Average yearly total of rain plus the water equivalent of snow, 1991–2020 normal.
basis: ECCC climate normal; annual total of daily precipitation

comparabilityNote: Values are for the climate station chosen to represent the place (flag station_proxy), not for the whole city. Stations differ in elevation, distance to water and urban setting. All use the 1991-2020 normals period.
label: Annual snowfall (1991–2020 normal)
description: Average yearly total snowfall (depth of fresh snow), 1991–2020 normal.
basis: ECCC climate normal; annual total snowfall in cm

comparabilityNote: Values are for the climate station chosen to represent the place (flag station_proxy), not for the whole city. Stations differ in elevation, distance to water and urban setting. All use the 1991-2020 normals period.
label: Days per year with minimum below −20 °C (1991–2020 normal)
description: Average number of days per year when the daily minimum temperature is below −20 °C, 1991–2020 normal.
basis: ECCC climate normal; days with minimum temperature < −20 °C

comparabilityNote: Values are for the climate station chosen to represent the place (flag station_proxy), not for the whole city. Stations differ in elevation, distance to water and urban setting. All use the 1991-2020 normals period.
label: Days per year with maximum above 30 °C (1991–2020 normal)
description: Average number of days per year when the daily maximum temperature exceeds 30 °C, 1991–2020 normal.
basis: ECCC climate normal; days with maximum temperature > 30 °C

label: Population estimate, July 1
description: Statistics Canada's annual postcensal population estimate for July 1 for the place's census metropolitan area / agglomeration (provincial part for Ottawa and Gatineau), on 2021 boundaries.
basis: Postcensal estimate based on the 2021 Census adjusted for net undercoverage, plus births, deaths and migration; all ages, both genders
comparabilityNote: Compares CMA/CA populations (not city-proper). Estimates are adjusted for census undercoverage, so they are higher than the 2021 Census counts. Iqaluit is not a CMA/CA and is not covered.
